narration: You think you're reading a menu. You're not. Cornell researchers found restaurants engineer every inch of it to make you spend more — and it works every time.
visual: Restaurant menu SVG with items listed (Salmon 28, Prime Rib 42, Halibut 38, Lobster 65). An eye appears on the menu at the end, staring back at the viewer.

narration: Your eyes always go to the same spot first — top right. Restaurants call it the golden triangle, and they plant their highest-margin items right there. You didn't pick that steak. The menu placed it in front of your eyes.
visual: Two-column menu. Right column glows amber and is labeled 'GOLDEN TRIANGLE.' An eye-tracking dot moves diagonally to land on top-right first.

narration: Cornell proved something wild: just removing the dollar sign increases spending by 8%. 'Salmon 42' feels way cheaper than 'Salmon $42' — your brain literally stops calculating.
visual: Two price cards side by side: one shows '$42' with a red strikethrough on the dollar sign, the other shows '42' glowing amber. Two comparison bars show spending level — the no-dollar bar is 8% longer.

narration: Here's the decoy play. That $72 lobster isn't there because anyone orders it — it's there to make the $38 steak look like a steal. This trick alone increases premium sales by 73%.
visual: Three menu items: cheap chicken at 26, filet mignon at 38 (gets highlighted in amber), and Japanese Wagyu at 72 labeled 'DECOY — exists to make $38 look cheap.'

narration: And the words. 'Chicken' costs 24. 'Slow-roasted, farm-fresh, hand-crafted chicken' costs 32. Same bird, better adjectives — and studies show descriptive language lifts perceived value by 27%.
visual: A plain dish name card shows 'Chicken — 24.' Three amber word-bubbles float in: SLOW-ROASTED, FARM-FRESH, HAND-CRAFTED. The price card updates to show 32 with a growing amber bar underneath.

narration: Americans eat out 5.9 times a week. Add up even $9.75 extra per engineered meal and you're handing restaurants over $3,000 a year in psychological tricks. Now you know — follow for more.
visual: Calculation breakdown: '307 meals/yr × +$9.75 = $3,000.' A piggy bank SVG sits beneath the math. Counter animates up to $3,000. CTA text: 'NOW YOU KNOW THE TRICKS — FOLLOW FOR MORE.'
